```text
## Found 2026-10-29: why some SpecStory files are truncated copies
Renaming a file inside `.specstory/history/` and then continuing that session makes SpecStory start a new, complete file under its own name; the renamed file stops growing. Don't rename files there; `/log-sync` gives the course names to the copies in `ai-logs/`. The earlier stale copies (`review-pr-94`, `understand-dod-and-check-issue-25`) may have the same cause, or were copied before the session ended.

## Settled: no forked skills
Tested 2026-10-29: SpecStory logs forked skills (as `Agent - sidechain`), but a fork costs about 75k tokens and hides its working from the main conversation. `/sprint-report` is a script in the main chat. "User" entries containing `<local-command-caveat>` or `<task-notification>` in logs are messages Claude Code adds automatically. Also still pending: copy this skill-building session (#12 in the `/log-sync` scan) once it ends.

# Issue #146 — handoff context for implementation planning

#146 = sub-issue 6 of #131 (OIDC sign-in): login/sign-up provider buttons + sign-in error messages. Owner: dchan01-wm.
Written 2026-11-18 from an earlier session's research (Nov 12) plus a fresh GitHub check. Code facts were traced at commit `e01d161c0c`-era `main`; re-check line numbers before editing.

| Full feature spec by Zach: 43 acceptance criteria, ADR-001..009, breakdown, Sprint 3 slice | PR #133, branch `docs/oidc-spec`, folder `specs/oidc-sign-in/` (`design.md`, `decisions.md`, `breakdown.md`, `implementation.md`, `customer-questions.md`, `future-work.md`). Not on `main`; read with `gh pr diff 133` or `git show origin/docs/oidc-spec:specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md` |
| Sub-issue 1 spec (data model + repository, `findEnabled()` DTO) | GitHub #136 |
| Course rules / sprint config | `.claude/course/skill-rules.md`, `.claude/course/current-sprint.md`, `.claude/course/sprint3-reference.md` |

The earlier session's overview of OIDC, the client's asks, and the phase estimates were given in chat only; the essentials are summarized below.

## How #131 is decomposed (Zach's breakdown, PR #133 `breakdown.md`)

| # | Sub-issue | Size | Depends on | Sprint | GitHub |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | OIDC provider table + `PrismaOidcProviderRepository` | M | — | 3 | #136 (zach-short), open, **no PR yet** |
| 2 | Local Keycloak test provider + realm + README | S | — | 3 | #151, open, **unassigned** |
| 3 | Admin provider service + tRPC (validation, secret encryption, discovery test, 10-provider cap) | M | 1 | 3 | not created |
| 4 | Admin "Identity providers" settings page | M | 3 | 3 | not created |
| 5 | Load providers per request in NextAuth (`oidc-<id>`) + `OidcSignInService` (new users, verified-email rule) | M | 1 | 3 | not created |
| 6 | **Login/sign-up buttons + sign-in error messages** | S | 1 (data), 5 (end to end) | 3 | **#146** |

Merge order: 1 → (3 ∥ 5) → (4 after 3, 6 after 5); 2 any time.

## What #146 must deliver (from the issue body)

1. **Buttons.** Login page: one "Continue with <display name>" per enabled provider, admin order, below Google/Microsoft, `signIn("oidc-<id>", { callbackUrl })`. Sign-up page: same, only providers with `allowSignup`, none when sign-up is disabled site-wide. No providers → pages unchanged. Only `id` + `displayName` reach the browser.
2. **Login-page errors.** Read `?error=`; translated messages for `OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback`, `AccessDenied`; generic fallback.
3. **`/auth/error` messages** for `missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists`, `unknown-provider`; OIDC name in `wrong-provider`.
All strings in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.
Feature-spec criteria it maps to: 11, 12, 21–25 in `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md`.

## Code facts (Confirmed by reading, Nov 12)

- `apps/web/server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx:88-93` — props `csrfToken`, `isGoogleLoginEnabled`, `isOutlookLoginEnabled: false`, `totpEmail`. Add `oidcProviders`.
- `apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx`
  - `:140`, `:255` — only `callbackUrl` / `email` read from the URL; `error` never read (existing bug, affects Google/Microsoft too).
  - `:131-137` — `errorMessages` map keyed by `ErrorCode`; `:161-170` credential-error handling.
  - `:173` — `showSocialLogin = isGoogleLoginEnabled || isOutlookLoginEnabled` → must include OIDC or an OIDC-only instance shows no buttons/divider.
  - `:198-214` Google button, `:215-230` Microsoft button (pattern: `setLastUsed`, `signIn`, `<LastUsed />`), then "or" divider.
- `apps/web/modules/auth/hooks/useLastUsed.tsx:7` — `type LoginType = "saml" | "google" | "microsoft" | "credentials"`; widen for `oidc-<id>`.
- `apps/web/lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx:58` — `isGoogleLoginEnabled`; add filtered `oidcProviders`.
- `apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx:197-198` props, `:632`, `:683`, `:734` Google/Microsoft/divider blocks.
- `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx:39-56` — `getErrorMessage` if/else chain; provider-name fallback "your original login method".
- Sign-up disabled = `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_SIGNUP === "true"` OR feature flag `disable-signup` (`apps/web/app/api/auth/signup/route.ts:29-31`). `login-view.tsx:175` checks only the env var.
- NextAuth 4.24.13; error page config `pages.error: "/auth/error"` in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (`pages` block ~L410). Providers are a static module-level array today (`:307-370`); per-request loading is sub-issue 5 (ADR-001).

## Contracts with other sub-issues

| Contract | With | Assumption #146 relies on |
|---|---|---|
| Data | #136 | `getOidcProviderRepository().findEnabled()` → `OidcProviderPublicDto` (`id`, `displayName`, `allowSignup`, …), ordered by `position`, no secret. DTO in `packages/lib/dto/`. |
| Provider id | sub-issue 5 | NextAuth provider id is `oidc-<id>` (`<id>` = OidcProvider cuid). |
| Error codes | sub-issue 5 | Sub-issue 5 emits the four `/auth/error` codes; #146 only displays them. |
| File overlap | #136 | #136 criterion 13 also edits `auth/error/page.tsx`; proposed that #146 owns it — confirm with Zach. |

## Open decisions (need ≥2 alternatives each in design, user chooses)

1. Where NextAuth OAuth errors show: login page reading `?error=` (issue's preference) vs `/auth/error` for everything.
2. Naming the failed provider in messages: generic text vs `lastUsed` value vs a parameter added by sub-issue 5.
3. How to build/merge before #136 exists: prop-driven buttons with the `findEnabled()` wiring as a last commit vs stacking on #136's branch vs a temporary local type.
4. Whether the sign-up page (criterion 12) is in this PR or split out.
5. Whether to extract a pure `code → translation key` helper (unit-testable; mutation-testing candidate for D6).
```

```text
### What does this PR do?

Adds the draft spec for #131 (sign in with any OIDC provider) and the Sprint 3 carryovers list. Documentation only; no product code.

### What changed

- `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md`: user story, scenario, 43 numbered acceptance criteria (main path, provider failures, unverified or missing email, existing-account conflicts, provider removal, lock-out, upgrade), and a proposed answer for each #131 open question, marked as needing customer confirmation.
- `specs/oidc-sign-in/decisions.md`: nine decisions, each with at least two alternatives and the reason for the choice. Account linking (ADR-004) is left to the customer.
- `specs/oidc-sign-in/customer-questions.md`: 13 numbered questions to post on #131. Q1 (account linking) and Q2 (who may sign up) block implementation.
- `specs/oidc-sign-in/breakdown.md`: nine sub-issues with size, dependencies and a blank owner column, plus a comment ready to post on #131.
- `specs/oidc-sign-in/implementation.md`: the Sprint 3 slice and merge order.
- `specs/oidc-sign-in/future-work.md`: deferred items.
- `docs/sprint3/carryovers.md`: open Sprint 2 items with owner and next step.

### Sprint 3 slice

An admin adds a Keycloak provider in admin settings (secret encrypted), the login page shows "Continue with <name>", a user with a verified email signs in and gets a new account, and an unverified email shows an error. A login whose email matches an existing account is rejected until the customer answers Q1. Merge order: sub-issue 1; then 3 and 5 in parallel; then 4 and 6; sub-issue 2 at any time.

### Review requests

- Fill the Owner column in `breakdown.md`.
- Check the customer questions before they go on #131.
- Account-linking path: a narrow security review of `signIn`, `jwt` and the adapter found that storing the OIDC `sub` in `User.identityProviderId` would allow a cross-provider collision. The rules it added are in ADR-005 and criteria 14, 28, 30, 31 and 34.

Nothing has been posted on #131 yet, and no sub-issues exist.
```

```text
This is sub-issue 1 of #131. It adds the storage for OIDC providers that an admin adds at run time, and the one repository that reads and writes it. It adds no UI, no tRPC route and no change to the login flow, so nothing a user sees changes.

- `schema.prisma` and one migration: the `OIDC` value on `IdentityProvider`, and the `OidcProvider` table with a unique pair of `issuer` and `clientId`.
- `PrismaOidcProviderRepository` (`packages/features/auth/oidc/repositories/`): `findEnabled`, `list`, `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret`, `create`, `update`, `setEnabled`, `countLinkedAccounts`, `deleteWithAccounts`.
- DTOs in `packages/lib/dto/OidcProviderDto.ts`. No method returns a Prisma type.
- DI: `getOidcProviderRepository()` in `packages/features/auth/oidc/di/`, built with `bindModuleToClassOnToken`.

## Design

The design decisions are in #136 (provider order, `allowedDomains` as a text array, the `Account` row as the user link, `updatedById` as a plain integer), each with its rejected alternatives. Three choices were made during the build and are not in the issue:

**Which error code a duplicate gets.** `ErrorCode` has no conflict value. A duplicate `issuer` and `clientId` becomes `ErrorWithCode` with `BadRequest` (HTTP 400). Adding a `Conflict` code was rejected because it changes a shared enum and `getHttpStatusCode` for one caller. Passing the Prisma error through was rejected because Prisma can print the failed write in its message, and that wri

hi @ojcchar, a few questions on #131 before we finish the spec. we put what we'd do next to each one, just tell us if that's fine or what you want instead. 1 and 2 block us.

1. if someone logs in with oidc and their email already has a cal.diy account, what should happen? we think auto link only if the admin says the provider owns that email domain, otherwise reject and make them link it from settings. never auto link an admin account.
2. who can make a new account through oidc? we think a per provider "allow new accounts" switch (off by default) plus an optional list of allowed domains. should the existing "disable signup" setting block oidc signup too?
3. if the provider doesn't send email_verified, we reject the login. ok?
4. do you want a switch to turn off password login? if so admins would always keep password login so nobody gets locked out. we'd do this in sprint 4.
5. if an admin removes a provider people use, we show how many users it affects, make them type the name to confirm, and those users can use forgot password to get back in. ok?
6. should the require 2fa setting apply to oidc users too, or does the provider's mfa count?
7. if someone's email changes at the provider, we update it in cal.diy if it's verified and not taken. ok?
8. if someone was invited but hasn't accepted yet, should an oidc login with that email take over the invite, or treat it like 1?
9. no mapping provider groups to cal.diy roles for now. ok?
10. users can unlink a provider unless it's their only way to log in. ok?
11. is up to 10 providers enough?
12. we're testing with keycloak locally. is that ok or do you want authentik or okta too?
13. after upgrading nothing changes until an admin adds a provider. ok?

thanks!

These are good questions, and your proposals are mostly what we want.

1. Agreed: auto-link only when the email is verified and the admin marked the provider as owning that domain. Otherwise reject and let the user link it from settings. Never auto-link admin accounts.
2. Agreed on the per-provider switch (off by default) and the allowed domains. Yes, the global "disable signup" setting also blocks OIDC sign-up, and it wins over the provider switch. An admin who turned off sign-up expects no new accounts from anywhere. They can still let people in by inviting them (see 8).
3. Yes, reject the login if email_verified is missing or false.
4. Yes, in Sprint 4. Admins always keep password login.
5. Fine, but check one thing: users created through OIDC have no password, so make sure "forgot password" actually works for them, and test it. Also let admins disable a provider instead of deleting it.
6. We'd like users to rely on the provider's MFA when it can be checked. Add a per-provider setting, "accept this provider's MFA." When it's on and the ID token's amr claim shows a second factor, skip Cal.diy's 2FA. If amr is missing or shows only a password, require Cal.diy's 2FA. This can be in Sprint 4.
7. Fine, as long as accounts are matched by the provider's user ID (the sub claim), never by email. If the new email is already taken, keep the old one and tell the user.
8. A verified OIDC login with an invited email accepts the invite, even if "allow new accounts" is off for that provider.
9. Agreed, no group mapping for now.
10. Agreed.
11. Yes, 10 is enough.
12. Keycloak is fine. Document the setup so anyone on the team can run the tests.
13. Agreed.
```

```text
Path: an admin adds one Keycloak provider in **Settings → Admin → Identity providers** (secret encrypted), the login page shows "Continue with <name>", a user with a verified email signs in against the local Keycloak and gets a new Cal.diy account, and a user with an unverified email sees the `unverified-email` message. A first login whose email matches an existing account is rejected with `oidc-account-exists`; that is the safe rule under every answer to Q1, so the slice does not wait on the customer.

Sub-issues on the path and merge order:

2026-11-09: a narrow Fable 5.1 review of the account-linking path (`signIn`, `jwt`, adapter, next-auth 4.24.13 callback order). Zach's status comment on #131 says so directly: "row 5 (the login flow) is the piece that connects the UI to the server."
```

## What's already taken

| # | Sub-issue | Owner | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Provider table + repository (#136) | zach-short | Draft PR #155 (+563 lines), not reviewed |
| 2 | Local Keycloak test setup (#151) | zachbowden | No PR |
| 3 | Admin service + tRPC (#152) | julissaehp | No PR |
| 6 | Login buttons + error messages (#146) | you | **PR #161 is approved but not merged** |
| 4 | Admin settings page | nobody | No issue |
| **5** | **Per-request providers + new-user sign-in** | **nobody** | **No issue** |
| 7–10 | Account linking, connected logins, removal, provider MFA | — | Planned for Sprint 4 |

The other open issues are assigned to other people or are large/stale backlog items (#14, #17, #18, #33). Nothing outside #131 is a better fit.

## Why #5 over #4
- Your #161 buttons call `signIn("oidc-<id>")`, but nothing registers those providers yet, so they can't do anything. #5 makes them work.
- #4 depends on #3, which has no PR. For a demo you can skip the admin page and insert a provider row with a seed script or SQL.

## Splitting it into two parts
Zach estimates ~450 lines including tests, so I'd split it:

- **5a: register providers on each request (~2 hours).**
  - Make `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts` async and load enabled providers through the #136 repository.
  - Build a next-auth `oauth` provider for each one: `wellKnown`, `idToken: true`, PKCE and state, 5-second timeout, no automatic email linking.
  - Map the `oidc-` prefix to `IdentityProvider.OIDC`.
  - Until 5b lands, `signIn` rejects OIDC logins.
  - With this, clicking your button reaches Keycloak and comes back.
- **5b: `OidcSignInService` (~2 hours or more).** One call from the top of `signIn` and one from the top of `jwt` in `next-auth-options.ts`. It would:
  - reject logins with an unverified or missing email;
  - create the user and the account link in one transaction;
  - find returning users by provider and the provider's user ID;
  - reject any login whose email matches an existing account with `oidc-account-exists`;
  - block new accounts when sign-up is disabled site-wide.

  The breakdown also asks for a narrow security review of the `signIn` and `jwt` changes before merge.

Realistically, 5a plus a tested 5b *service* (unit tests only, wiring possibly unfinished) fits in 4 hours. Everything working end to end in 4 hours is optimistic.

## Risks to raise with the team
1. **Everything depends on #155**, which is still an unreviewed draft. Build 5a on top of Zach's branch `feat/issue-136-oidc-provider-repository`, or ask Zach to merge first.
2. **The repository can't load secrets in bulk.** `findEnabled()` returns `OidcProviderPublicDto`, which has no client secret, and the only method that returns one fetches a single provider by id. 5a needs a new `findEnabledWithEncryptedSecret()` (a change to Zach's PR) or one lookup per provider.
3. **The demo also needs a local Keycloak (#151, no PR).** Ask zachbowden for the realm file early.
4. **#161 is approved but not merged.** Merging it reduces the stack.

**5b would be a medium issue on its own. 5a is on the line between small and medium.** The course reference doesn't define the sizes, so I'm comparing with the team's own usage. #146 was sized medium at 7–9 files and 200–300 lines, and the breakdown's other medium issues run about 250–450 lines.

## 5a: register providers on each request (borderline small/medium)
Estimated 4–6 files, ~200–250 lines with tests:
- Make the NextAuth route async and pass the loaded providers into `getOptions` (~20 lines).
- A pure builder that turns a provider record into a next-auth `oauth` provider with discovery, PKCE, state, timeout and secret decryption (~60 lines).
- A repository method that returns enabled providers with their secrets, or the same change made in Zach's #155 (~20 lines).
- Map the `oidc-` prefix to `IdentityProvider.OIDC`, and stop `signIn` from accepting OIDC logins for now (~20 lines).
- Unit tests for the builder and the mapping (~100 lines).

By line count it's close to small. I'd still call it **medium** because of the risk: it changes the entry point every login goes through, depends on next-auth internals (async options in the Pages Router route), and handles a decrypted secret. If you want it clearly medium, move the "reject OIDC in `signIn`" guard and its test from 5b into 5a. That also makes 5a safe to merge alone, because a half-configured provider can't sign anyone in.

## 5b: `OidcSignInService` (clearly medium, close to large)
Estimated 5–7 files, ~300–400 lines with tests:
- The service handles about seven branches: unverified email, missing email, name fallback, sign-up allowed or blocked (including the site-wide switch), new user plus account link in one transaction, returning user found by provider and user ID, and existing-email rejection.
- It needs a repository method for the transaction, DI wiring, and the two calls from `signIn` and `jwt`.
- Testing every branch, plus the two-providers-same-user-ID case, takes the most lines.
- It needs a narrow security review before merge.

## For your 4 hours
5a fits comfortably. 5b alone is a full medium issue, likely more than the ~2 hours left after 5a. Aim to finish 5a and get the 5b service and its unit tests done; connecting it to `signIn` and `jwt` may slip.

```text
## User Story

As a cal.diy administrator, I want to configure, validate, test, and manage OIDC identity providers so that users can securely authenticate through external identity providers without exposing sensitive credentials or enabling invalid configurations.

## User Scenario

An administrator wants to configure Keycloak as an external identity provider for cal.diy. They enter the provider's display name, issuer URL, client ID, client secret, scopes, and account creation settings.

The backend validates the configuration and encrypts the client secret before saving the provider. The provider is initially disabled, and no client secret is exposed in the response.

The administrator tests the connection and enables the provider after a successful result. If the administrator later needs to stop using the provider, they can disable it without removing existing users' account links.

If a provider has linked users, the administrator is temporarily prevented from deleting it until the account recovery functionality has been implemented and tested.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Admin Access

- [ ] Provide admin-only tRPC procedures under `viewer.admin.oidcProviders`: `list`, `create`, `update`, `setEnabled`, `delete`, and `testDiscovery`. All procedures use `authedAdminProcedure`. Non-administrators receive `FORBIDDEN` without accessing or modifying provider data.

### Provider Configuration and Validation

- [ ] Support the required provider configuration fields: `displayName`, `issuer`, `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `scopes`, `allowSignup`, `allowedDomains`, and `position`. New providers are disabled by default, with scopes defaulting to `openid email profile`, `allowSignup` to `false`, and `allowedDomains` to `[]`.

- [ ] Validate provider configurations:
  - Display names are trimmed and contain 1–50 characters.
  - Issuer URLs require HTTPS, except that HTTP is accepted for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and hosts ending in `.localhost`.
  - Client IDs and newly created client secrets cannot be empty.
  - Scopes must include `openid`.
  - Allowed domains are valid, lowercase, and unique; an empty list means no restriction.
  - Invalid fields return field-specific validation errors without saving changes.

- [ ] Enforce a maximum of 10 providers and prevent duplicate issuer and client ID combinations.

- [ ] Do not introduce settings that bypass email verification or map external groups or claims to cal.diy roles.

### Client Secret Encryption

- [ ] Encrypt client secrets using the existing `symmetricEncrypt` utility and `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` before persistence. Neither plaintext nor encrypted secrets are exposed in responses, logs, or errors.

- [ ] Preserve the existing secret when no new secret is supplied or the secret field is empty during an update. Replace it when a new secret is supplied.

- [ ] Return meaningful errors when the encryption key is missing or invalid, while allowing operations that do not require secret encryption to continue.

### Provider Management

- [ ] Support provider management through the repository introduced in #136. Provider responses exclude secrets and include configuration details, timestamps, and callback URLs in the format `<WEBAPP_URL>/api/auth/callback/oidc-<id>`.

- [ ] List providers by `position`, then `createdAt`. Concurrent updates preserve the most recent successful change and record the responsible administrator through `updatedById`. Operations targeting nonexistent providers return `NOT_FOUND`.

### Connection Testing

- [ ] Test the provider's discovery endpoint using a server-side request with a five-second timeout. Return one of the following results:
  - `unreachable`: Network, DNS, or timeout failure.
  - `not_discovery_document`: Invalid HTTP response, JSON, or missing required endpoints.
  - `issuer_mismatch`: The returned issuer does not match the configured issuer.
  - `unsupported_flow`: The required authorization code flow is not supported.
  - `ok`: All required discovery checks pass.

- [ ] Connection testing does not require client secrets or modify stored provider configurations. Saving a valid configuration does not require a successful connection test.

### Enabling, Disabling, and Deleting Providers

- [ ] Enabling a provider requires a successful server-side discovery check. A failed check leaves the provider disabled and returns the corresponding connection result.

- [ ] Disabling a provider preserves its configuration and existing user account links.

- [ ] Allow deletion of providers without linked users. As an interim safeguard, reject deletion when linked users exist, report the number of linked users, and suggest disabling the provider instead.

### Testing and Regression

- [ ] Automated tests cover validation, encryption, secret preservation, all discovery outcomes, authorization, provider limits, and provider management.

- [ ] Existing authentication and sign-up behavior remain unchanged when no providers are configured. No providers are created automatically.

- [ ] Relevant regression tests, Biome checks, and TypeScript type-checking pass.

## Out of Scope

- OIDC provider database models and repository implementation (#136).
- Local Keycloak testing environment setup (#151).
- Admin identity provider settings interface.
- OIDC authentication and new-user account creation.
- Login buttons and sign-in error messages (#146).
- Enforcement of account creation and email verification rules during authentication.
- Linking OIDC providers to existing user accounts.
- Connected login management.
- Full deletion of providers with linked users, including typed confirmation, only-login counts, and account recovery testing.
- Per-provider MFA configuration.
- Password-login configuration.
- Group-to-role mapping.
- Verifying client credentials during connection testing.

## Open Questions

- Should allowed domains for account creation and owned domains for automatic account linking use the same configuration field or separate fields?

- How should the callback URL be generated before the provider is initially saved, given that the URL depends on the provider's ID?

- If an administrator changes the issuer URL or client ID of an already enabled provider, should the system require a successful connection test, automatically disable the provider, or allow the update without additional validation?

## Design Decisions

### Separate provider service from API procedures

**Alternatives considered:**

- Implement validation, encryption, connection testing, and provider management directly inside the tRPC procedures.
- Implement reusable backend service functionality separately from the tRPC procedures.

**Chosen approach:**

Create a reusable `OidcProviderService` that handles provider management and business logic separately from the admin tRPC procedures.

**Rationale:**

This separates business logic from API handling, improves testability, reduces duplication, and allows database-independent functionality to be implemented before #136 is completed.

### Reuse existing encryption functionality
```

```text
 * Maps NextAuth provider names to IdentityProvider enum values.
 * Includes aliases (e.g., "saml-idp" -> SAML).
 */
export const NEXTAUTH_TO_IDENTITY_PROVIDER: Record<string, IdentityProvider> = {
  "azure-ad": IdentityProvider.AZUREAD,

  saml: IdentityProvider.SAML,
  "saml-idp": IdentityProvider.SAML,
```

```text
5:## ADR-001: How providers reach NextAuth without a restart
6-
7-Status: Proposed.
8-
9-### Context
10-
11-Today `providers` is a module-level array built once at import (`next-auth-options.ts:307–370`), and `getOptions` is synchronous. Criterion 1 requires a change to take effect on the next login with no restart. `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts` already calls `NextAuth(req, res, getOptions(...))` on every request, so options can differ per request.
12-
13-### Options Considered
14-
15-1. **Load enabled providers from the database on each `/api/auth/*` request.** The handler awaits a repository call, then passes the result to `getOptions`. Pros: always current, no invalidation logic, correct on several server instances. Cons: one indexed query per auth request (sign-in, callback, session, CSRF). Auth traffic is small next to booking traffic, and the table holds at most 10 rows.
16-2. **Cache providers in memory with invalidation on admin save.** Pros: no query on most requests. Cons: each server instance has its own cache, so a save on instance A is stale on instance B until a TTL expires; this breaks criterion 1 on any multi-instance deploy unless we add Redis pub/sub. More code to review.
17-3. **Build providers at boot from the database.** Pros: no change to `getOptions`. Cons: needs a restart, which fails criterion 1.
```

```markdown
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

#146 adds a "Continue with <name>" button for each OIDC provider an admin has added. Each button calls `signIn("oidc-<id>")`, but NextAuth doesn't know about any of these providers. Its provider list is a module-level array built once at import (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:307`), and it only holds credentials, Google, Microsoft and email. Clicking an OIDC button can't start a sign-in, and a provider an admin adds later can't be used without restarting the server.

This is sub-issue **5a** of #131. Sub-issue 5 in the breakdown (PR #133, `specs/oidc-sign-in/breakdown.md`) is split in two so each part can be reviewed and merged on its own:

- **5a (this issue):** register enabled OIDC providers with NextAuth on each auth request, and reject every OIDC sign-in safely until 5b exists.
- **5b (next issue):** `OidcSignInService`, which decides who may sign in, creates new users and finds returning users. 5b replaces the rejection added here.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Load the enabled providers from the database on each `/api/auth/*` request and pass them to NextAuth (ADR-001, option 1). Until 5b lands, every OIDC sign-in is rejected in `signIn` before any account lookup or write. That makes this PR safe to merge alone.

**Changes**

1. `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts`: make the handler async. Load enabled providers through `getOidcProviderRepository()` (#136), then pass them to `getOptions`.
2. `getOptions` takes an optional `dynamicProviders: Provider[]` (default `[]`) and appends it after the existing providers. Other callers (`apps/web/lib/settings/license-key/new/getServerSideProps.tsx`) keep working unchanged.
3. A pure builder (`buildOidcProvider`) turns one provider record into a next-auth `type: "oauth"` provider:
   - `id: "oidc-<id>"`, `name: displayName`
   - `wellKnown: <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`, `idToken: true`, `checks: ["pkce", "state"]`
   - `httpOptions: { timeout: 5000 }`
   - `authorization.params.scope` from the provider's `scopes`
   - client secret decrypted with `symmetricDecrypt` (`packages/lib/crypto.ts:31`) and `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`
   - **no** `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking`
4. `packages/features/auth/lib/identityProviders.ts`: `getIdentityProvider` maps any `oidc-*` provider id to `IdentityProvider.OIDC` (enum value added in #136).
5. **Temporary guard:** at the top of the `signIn` callback, before `getIdentityProvider` and every lookup, an `oidc-*` provider returns `"/auth/error?error=unknown-provider"`. next-auth 4 calls `signIn` before the adapter creates a user or links an account, so a rejected login writes nothing. 5b replaces this guard with the call to `OidcSignInService`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With one enabled provider, `GET /api/auth/providers` lists `oidc-<id>` with its display name, and clicking its button on the login page redirects to the provider's authorization endpoint with `code_challenge` and `state` parameters.
- [ ] Disabled providers aren't registered. Enabling or disabling a provider takes effect on the next request with no restart (#131 criterion 1).
- [ ] When the provider sends the user back, the sign-in is rejected and the user lands on `/auth/error?error=unknown-provider`. No `User` or `Account` row is created and no existing user is signed in or changed. It also can't reach the shared `identityProvider` lookups, the "verified and not CAL" branch, or `autoMergeIdentities()` (#131 criterion 28, interim form).
- [ ] The registered provider object has no `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking`, and the decrypted secret is never logged or returned. `/api/auth/providers` exposes only id, name, type and URLs.
- [ ] If loading providers fails (database error) or one provider's secret can't be decrypted (missing or wrong `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), that provider (or all OIDC providers) is skipped with a warning that doesn't include the secret. Password, Google, Microsoft and email login keep working.
- [ ] An unreachable issuer doesn't slow down the login page or other sign-in methods: discovery is fetched only when that provider's sign-in starts, with a 5-second timeout.
- [ ] With no providers configured, NextAuth behaves exactly as it does today (#131 criterion 13 / customer answer 13).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: the builder (id, discovery URL, checks, scopes, timeout, no dangerous linking); `getIdentityProvider` for `oidc-*` and the existing providers; the `signIn` guard (rejects and returns the error URL before any lookup); the handler (enabled providers passed to `getOptions`, failed load falls back to the built-in providers, a bad secret skips only that provider).
- [ ] `yarn turbo run type-check --filter=@calcom/web --filter=@calcom/features --force`, Biome and the touched unit tests pass.

**Out of scope**

- Sign-in decisions, new users, returning users, email rules and the `jwt` callback changes (5b).
- Linking OIDC to existing accounts (sub-issue 7, Sprint 4).
- Admin service, tRPC and settings page (#152, sub-issue 4).
- Login buttons and error messages (#146, PR #161).
- Local Keycloak realm (#151); the end-to-end demo needs it.
- Any change to Google or Microsoft login.

**Depends on:** #136 / PR #155 (`OidcProvider` table, `IdentityProvider.OIDC`, repository). Blocks 5b.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

**How providers reach NextAuth** (decided in ADR-001, PR #133)

- *Load from the database on each auth request (chosen).* Always current, works with several server instances, no cache invalidation. It costs one indexed query on a table of at most 10 rows per `/api/auth/*` request.
- *In-memory cache invalidated on admin save.* Fewer queries, but each server instance has its own cache, so a change is stale on other instances. Rejected.
- *Build providers once at boot.* Needs a restart after every admin change, which fails #131 criterion 1. Rejected.

**How to read secrets for all enabled providers**

- *Add `findEnabledWithEncryptedSecret()` to `PrismaOidcProviderRepository` (preferred).* One query. It's a small addition to #136's repository, either in PR #155 (ask Zach) or in this PR.
- *`findEnabled()` and then `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret(id)` for each provider.* Uses only existing methods but adds up to 10 extra queries on every auth request.
- *Decrypt inside the repository and return plaintext.* Rejected: the secret would cross into more layers, and repositories shouldn't contain logic.

**Keeping 5a safe to merge alone**

- *Reject every `oidc-*` login at the top of `signIn` (chosen).* One early return, easy to test, and 5b replaces it.
- *Register providers but leave the existing `signIn` logic to handle them.* Rejected: once `oidc-*` maps to `IdentityProvider.OIDC`, a login falls into the existing branches. These include the "verified and not CAL" branch, which can sign into an existing account by email (#131 criterion 28).
- *Don't map `oidc-*` to an `IdentityProvider` yet.* The existing `unknown-provider` rejection would catch it in `signIn`. It's fragile, though: the `jwt` callback falls back to `autoMergeIdentities()` for unknown providers, so safety would rest on callback order instead of an explicit guard.

### Additional context

- Parent: #131. Sibling sub-issues: #136 (data), #151 (Keycloak), #152 (admin service), #146 (buttons and errors).
- Customer answers on #131 (2026-11-12) that apply: 3 (reject when `email_verified` is missing or false, enforced in 5b) and 13 (no visible change until a provider is added).
- The breakdown asks for a narrow security review of the `signIn` and `jwt` changes in sub-issue 5. For 5a that's only the guard; the full review applies to 5b.

**Open questions**

1. Should the temporary rejection reuse `unknown-provider`, or get its own code such as `oidc-not-available` with a message added to `/auth/error`? Reusing it avoids a new translation string that 5b would delete.
2. Every `/api/auth/session` request also runs the provider query. Should the query run only for the `providers`, `signin` and `callback` actions? That saves a query on session polling but adds a routing rule that has to stay in sync with next-auth.
3. Does `httpOptions.timeout` apply to the discovery fetch in next-auth 4.24.13, or only to the token and userinfo calls? This needs checking during implementation (design.md marks it "to confirm").

### Requirement/Document

- Feature spec: PR #133, `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md` (criteria 1, 13, 28; Technical Design, "Each provider becomes a NextAuth `type: \"oauth\"` provider…"), `decisions.md` (ADR-001, ADR-005), `breakdown.md` (sub-issue 5).
- next-auth 4 OAuth provider options: https://next-auth.js.org/configuration/providers/oauth

```

```text
## User Story
As a self-hosted Cal.diy administrator, I want every OIDC provider I enable to be usable for sign-in on the next request, without restarting the server, while every OIDC sign-in is safely refused until account handling (5b) is ready so that I can check that my provider is wired up correctly (the button reaches my provider's login page and comes back), and no account can be created, changed or taken over by a sign-in flow that is only half finished.
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```markdown
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

#146 adds a "Continue with <name>" button for each OIDC provider an admin has added. Each button calls `signIn("oidc-<id>")`, but NextAuth doesn't know about any of these providers. Its provider list is a module-level array built once at import (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:307`), and it only holds credentials, Google, Microsoft and email. Clicking an OIDC button can't start a sign-in, and a provider an admin adds later can't be used without restarting the server.

This is sub-issue **5a** of #131. Sub-issue 5 in the breakdown (PR #133, `specs/oidc-sign-in/breakdown.md`) is split in two so each part can be reviewed and merged on its own:

- **5a (this issue):** register enabled OIDC providers with NextAuth on each auth request, and reject every OIDC sign-in safely until 5b exists.
- **5b (next issue):** `OidcSignInService`, which decides who may sign in, creates new users and finds returning users. 5b replaces the rejection added here.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Load the enabled providers from the database on each `/api/auth/*` request and pass them to NextAuth (ADR-001, option 1). Until 5b lands, every OIDC sign-in is rejected in `signIn` before any account lookup or write, which makes this PR safe to merge alone. Behavior is specified in **Acceptance Criteria** below; the planned changes are:

1. `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts`: make the handler async. Load enabled providers through `getOidcProviderRepository()` (#136), then pass them to `getOptions`.
2. `getOptions` takes an optional `dynamicProviders: Provider[]` (default `[]`) and appends it after the existing providers.
3. A pure builder (`buildOidcProvider`) turns one provider record into a next-auth `type: "oauth"` provider: `id: "oidc-<id>"`, `wellKnown`, `idToken: true`, `checks: ["pkce", "state"]`, `httpOptions: { timeout: 5000 }`, the provider's scopes, the secret decrypted with `symmetricDecrypt`, and **no** `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking`.
4. `packages/features/auth/lib/identityProviders.ts`: `getIdentityProvider` maps any `oidc-*` provider id to `IdentityProvider.OIDC` (enum value added in #136).
5. **Temporary guard** at the top of the `signIn` callback: an `oidc-*` provider returns `"/auth/error?error=unknown-provider"`. 5b replaces it with the call to `OidcSignInService`.

**Depends on:** #136 / PR #155 (`OidcProvider` table, `IdentityProvider.OIDC`, repository). Blocks 5b.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

**How providers reach NextAuth** (decided in ADR-001, PR #133)

- *Load from the database on each auth request (chosen).* Always current, works with several server instances, no cache invalidation. It costs one indexed query on a table of at most 10 rows per `/api/auth/*` request.
- *In-memory cache invalidated on admin save.* Fewer queries, but each server instance has its own cache, so a change is stale on other instances. Rejected.
- *Build providers once at boot.* Needs a restart after every admin change, which fails #131 criterion 1. Rejected.

**How to read secrets for all enabled providers**

- *Add `findEnabledWithEncryptedSecret()` to `PrismaOidcProviderRepository` (preferred).* One query. It's a small addition to #136's repository, either in PR #155 (ask Zach) or in this PR.
- *`findEnabled()` and then `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret(id)` for each provider.* Uses only existing methods but adds up to 10 extra queries on every auth request.
- *Decrypt inside the repository and return plaintext.* Rejected: the secret would cross into more layers, and repositories shouldn't contain logic.

**Keeping 5a safe to merge alone**

- *Reject every `oidc-*` login at the top of `signIn` (chosen).* One early return, easy to test, and 5b replaces it.
- *Register providers but leave the existing `signIn` logic to handle them.* Rejected: once `oidc-*` maps to `IdentityProvider.OIDC`, a login falls into the existing branches. These include the "verified and not CAL" branch (`next-auth-options.ts:1012`), which can sign into an existing account by email (#131 criterion 28).
- *Don't map `oidc-*` to an `IdentityProvider` yet.* The existing `unknown-provider` rejection would catch it in `signIn` (`next-auth-options.ts:855-861`). It's fragile, though: the `jwt` callback falls back to `autoMergeIdentities()` for unknown providers (`next-auth-options.ts:592-598`), so safety would rest on callback order instead of an explicit guard.

### Additional context

- Parent: #131. Sibling sub-issues: #136 (data), #151 (Keycloak), #152 (admin service), #146 (buttons and errors).
- Customer answers on #131 (2026-11-12) that apply: 3 (reject when `email_verified` is missing or false, enforced in 5b) and 13 (no visible change until a provider is added).
```

> **User Story:** As a self-hosted Cal.diy administrator, I want every OIDC provider I enable to be usable for sign-in on the next request, without restarting the server, while every OIDC sign-in is safely refused until account handling (5b) is ready so that I can check that my provider is wired up correctly (the button reaches my provider's login page and comes back), and no account can be created, changed or taken over by a sign-in flow that is only half finished.

| What changes | `findEnabledWithEncryptedSecret(): Promise<OidcProviderWithEncryptedSecretDto[]>` plus a test, in Zach's PR. | The same method and test, added by you to the repository after #155 merges, or on top of Zach's branch. | `findEnabled()`, then `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret(id)` for each provider. |
| Pros | One query; the repository stays in one PR with one owner. | One query; you don't wait on Zach. | No repository change at all. |
| Cons / risks | Depends on Zach's time on the last day; his PR has to change again. | Changes a file Zach owns, so there's a merge-order and conflict risk if #155 is still changing. | Up to 11 queries per `/api/auth/*` request. A provider disabled between the two reads is still loaded, because the second method doesn't check `enabled`. |
| Rules | Repository naming fits `data-repository-methods.md` (team). | Same. | Goes against `performance-avoid-quadratic.md` in spirit: one query per provider on a hot path (team). |

## Decision 3: What the temporary refusal returns

**Context:** The guard at the top of `signIn` (`next-auth-options.ts:808`, Confirmed) must refuse every `oidc-*` sign-in. Whatever it returns is what the user sees. The error page messages are in #161's `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/authErrorMessages.ts`, which is approved but not merged.

| | **A. Reuse `unknown-provider`** | **B. New code `oidc-not-available`** | **C. Return `false`** |
|---|---|---|---|
| What changes | `return "/auth/error?error=unknown-provider"` | A new code, a new string in `common.json`, and a mapping added to #161's error-message module. | `return false`, which next-auth turns into `/auth/error?error=AccessDenied` (`next-auth/core/routes/callback.js:85`, Confirmed). |
| Pros | The message already exists, in #161 and in today's code (`next-auth-options.ts:861`). Nothing to remove later. | The message can say what's really happening ("not available yet"). | Simplest code. |
| Cons / risks | The message ("this sign-in method is not available") is slightly vague for an admin testing it. | This PR then depends on #161, and the string becomes dead once 5b lands, so 5b has to remove it. | "Access denied" is misleading: it sounds like the provider refused the user. |
| Tests | One assertion on the returned URL. | Plus a mapping test. | One assertion. |

---

### Smaller choices

**4. The 5-second timeout.** openid-client's timeout default is shared by the whole server process (`request.js:17,33-43`, Confirmed). Setting a timeout on an OIDC provider (`client.js:10`, Confirmed) therefore also changes it for Google and Microsoft once any OIDC sign-in has run.
- **A. Set `httpOptions: { timeout: 5000 }` as the feature spec says.** Matches design.md, but raises the timeout for every provider from 3.5 s to 5 s. Which value applies depends on whether an OIDC sign-in has happened yet.
- **B. Leave `httpOptions` unset and keep the 3.5 s default.** No side effect, and it still meets acceptance criterion 8 ("within about 5 seconds"). It doesn't match the feature spec's literal 5000, so you'd post a note on #131.

**5. Which requests load providers.** ADR-001 already chose "every request".
- **A. Every `/api/auth/*` request, as ADR-001 says.** Simple, but `/api/auth/session` runs the query on every session check.
- **B. Only the `providers`, `signin` and `callback` actions.** Saves the session-check query, but adds a rule that breaks if next-auth needs providers on another action.

### Skipped (one sensible answer)
- **The provider id format:** reuse `getOidcAccountProviderId` from #155; writing it a second time would let the two drift apart.
- **The `oidc-*` → `IdentityProvider.OIDC` mapping:** a prefix check inside `getIdentityProvider` (`identityProviders.ts:19-21`). The existing exact-key table can't hold dynamic ids.
- **Where the guard goes:** it has to be the first check for `oidc-*` in `signIn`, before line 855, or criterion 3 fails.

---

**Please choose an option for decisions 1–3, and for 4–5 if you want those recorded, and give your reasons in your own words.** Your reasons become the Rationale in `design.md`. If you'd like my recommendation, ask and I'll give it with how confident I am.

```text
## Design

Design decisions for #146 (sub-issue 6 of #131). Each follows the course template.

### Decision 1: Where error-code messages live

**Decision:** Map sign-in error codes to translation keys in one shared pure module, `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/authErrorMessages.ts`, used by both the login page and `/auth/error`.

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Shared pure module (chosen): `getLoginErrorKey(code)` and `getAuthErrorPageMessage(code, provider)` return i18n keys and parameters; `login-view.tsx` and `auth/error/page.tsx` call them, and a `.test.ts` file covers every code plus an unknown one.
2. Extend each page in place: add entries to the `errorMessages` map in `login-view.tsx` (`:131-137`) and new branches to the if/else chain in `auth/error/page.tsx` (`:36-56`).
3. Add NextAuth's codes (`OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback`, …) to the `ErrorCode` enum in `packages/features/auth/lib/ErrorCode.ts` and look them up in the login page's existing map.

**Rationale:** It keeps the mapping in one place that a unit test can reach and avoids duplicating the logic across two pages. A pure function can be tested with plain inputs. Logic left inside the views would need component tests with rendering and mocks, and the `/auth/error` server page under `apps/web/app/` has no Vitest project that collects its tests (`vitest.workspace.ts` only collects `.tsx` tests from `apps/web/modules/**` and `apps/web/components/**`, `:158`, `:188`), so its logic could only be checked manually; the enum option would put web-only NextAuth codes into `packages/features` and still not help `/auth/error`.

**Consequences:** Easier: unit tests for acceptance criteria 6–8, a clear target for StrykerJS mutation testing (D6), and adding future codes in one place. Harder: one new file and one more level of indirection; the pages still need a manual check that they display the returned key.

### Decision 2: How providers reach the pages before #136

**Decision:** Pass providers to the login and sign-up pages as an `oidcProviders` prop of `{ id, displayName }` built by a pure mapper, with the props set to `[]` until #136 merges and the `findEnabled()` call added as a final commit.

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Props + mapper now, wire later (chosen): add `OidcLoginButton` (`{ id, displayName }`) and `toOidcLoginButtons(providers, { signup })`, which filters by `allowSignup` and drops every other field; `server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx` and `lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx` pass the result; the input type temporarily copies the shape of #136's `OidcProviderPublicDto`.
2. Stack on #136's branch: import the real DTO and `getOidcProviderRepository()` and call `findEnabled()` in the server props from the start.
3. Fetch on the client: add a public tRPC query or API route that returns the button list and load it in the views on mount.

**Rationale:** It lets the PR open and be tested today without waiting for #136, which has no branch yet, and the mapper is a `.ts` unit that tests acceptance criteria 3–5 directly. Stacking is blocked on #136, and a client fetch adds a new public endpoint and a layout shift for no benefit.

**Consequences:** Easier: an independent, small PR with unit-tested filtering and field stripping. Harder: the temporary input type must be replaced with #136's DTO and the `findEnabled()` call added after #136 merges (recorded under Tech Debt → Introduced); until then no buttons appear on any instance.
```

```text
Template 3 "design-decision" (suggested): 5/5 fixed parts found — OK
5
## Design

Design decisions for #164 (sub-issue 5a of #131). Each follows the course template.

### Decision 1: Where provider loading and building lives

**Decision:** Keep the route handler thin and put provider construction in a pure builder: `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/buildOidcProvider.ts` turns one provider record into a next-auth `Provider`, and `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts` loads the records through `getOidcProviderRepository()`, skips any provider whose secret fails to decrypt, falls back to the built-in providers if loading fails, and passes the result to `getOptions({ ..., dynamicProviders })`.

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Thin handler + pure builder (chosen): a new `buildOidcProvider.ts` plus its unit test; the async handler holds the load, skip and fallback logic; `getOptions` gains an optional `dynamicProviders: Provider[] = []` argument (~4–5 files, ~200 lines).
2. Service with dependency injection: an `OidcNextAuthProviderService` with `loadProviders(): Promise<Provider[]>`, plus a module, a container and tokens in `packages/features/auth/oidc/`, with the repository injected; the handler only awaits the service (~7–8 files, ~260 lines).
3. Async `getOptions`: `getOptions` loads and builds the providers itself and returns `Promise<AuthOptions>`; every caller awaits it.

**Rationale:** It is the easiest option to implement and to test: the builder is a pure function that unit tests (and StrykerJS) can exercise with plain inputs, and it adds the fewest files on the last day of the sprint. The trade-off, that the skip and fallback logic in the Pages API route is harder to unit-test, is accepted and recorded as tech debt. Making `getOptions` async was rejected because it breaks the synchronous caller in `apps/web/lib/settings/license-key/new/getServerSideProps.tsx:10` and 8 test call sites, and grows the 1,255-line `next-auth-options.ts`.

**Consequences:** Easier: a small PR, a pure builder covered directly by unit and mutation tests, and no change to existing `getOptions` callers. Harder: the handler's skip-on-bad-secret and fallback-on-load-failure logic lives in `apps/web` and needs a test that mocks `NextAuth`, the repository and `req`/`res` (recorded under Tech Debt → Introduced); if a second caller ever needs OIDC providers (for example the App Router), the loading logic would have to move into a service.

### Decision 2: How the client secrets are read

**Decision:** Read secrets with the repository methods that already exist in #136 / PR #155: `findEnabled()` for the list, then `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret(id)` for each enabled provider, without changing the repository.
```

Yes. The usual way is to make 5a depend on a small interface it defines itself instead of on #155's code. The real repository gets plugged in later with a one-line change. It's the same approach your #146 PR (#161) took: providers are `[]` until #136 lands.

## What 5a needs from #155 today

| From #155 | Where 5a uses it | Without #155 |
|---|---|---|
| Repository and DI container (`getOidcProviderRepository()`) | Loading providers in the handler | Define a small source interface in 5a; use an empty source until #155 merges |
| DTO types (`OidcProviderPublicDto`, …) | Input type of the builder | A local input type with the fields the builder needs (id, displayName, issuer, clientId, encrypted secret, scopes) |
| `getOidcAccountProviderId(id)` | Builds `oidc-<id>` | A one-line local helper; dedupe after #155 merges |
| `IdentityProvider.OIDC` enum value (schema change) | Acceptance criterion 5 (the `oidc-*` mapping) | Move the mapping to the wiring step or to 5b |

Dropping the enum mapping for now is still safe. The `signIn` guard checks the `oidc-` prefix itself and runs first. next-auth only calls `jwt` when `signIn` allows the login (`callback.js:78`), so the `autoMergeIdentities()` fallback for unknown providers in `jwt` can't be reached.

## The approach
- `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/buildOidcProvider.ts`: a pure builder, with a local input type.
- `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/loadOidcNextAuthProviders.ts`: `loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source)`.
  - `source` is an interface like `{ findEnabled(); findByIdWithEncryptedSecret(id) }`, matching #155's method names. Wiring is then just passing the repository, and Decision 2 still holds.
  - It holds the decrypt, skip-bad-secret and fallback logic.
- The handler calls it with an empty source for now. After #155 merges, a one-line change swaps in `getOidcProviderRepository()`.
- The `signIn` guard, the `getOptions({ dynamicProviders })` argument and the tests ship as planned.

**A bonus:** this also mostly clears the tech debt from Decision 1. The skip and fallback logic moves out of the hard-to-test route into a function you can test with a fake source.

## What you give up
- **No visible behavior change until the wiring lands.** In production the source is empty, so the provider list is unchanged. Criteria 1, 2 and 8 are proven by unit tests with a fake source, not manually with Keycloak. Realistically, the end-to-end demo isn't possible this sprint either way, because #155, #151 and #152 are all unmerged.
- **A temporary local type** that has to match #155's DTO. TypeScript catches any mismatch at wiring time; record it in Tech Debt → Introduced.
- **Criterion 5 moves out** of this PR.

## Other ways (I'd advise against them)
- **Copy #155's schema and migration into this PR.** Two PRs would add the same table and migration, guaranteeing conflicts and possibly a double migration.
- **Configure a test provider from environment variables.** That would give a working Keycloak demo without the database, but it's throwaway code in the auth path, and the customer asked for runtime configuration, not configuration from environment variables.

## If you go ahead, these files change
- **`spec.md`**: criterion 5 moves out, criteria 1, 2 and 8 become "with a provider source", and a wiring step is added under Out of Scope (or as a follow-up).
- **`design.md`**: a new Decision 6, "independence from #155", with the three options above. Decision 1's Consequences get updated, and Decision 2 becomes "applied at wiring time".
- **`tech-debt-notes.md`**: the local type and the pending wiring.

Should I update those three files this way?

```markdown
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

#146 adds a "Continue with <name>" button for each OIDC provider an admin has added. Each button calls `signIn("oidc-<id>")`, but NextAuth doesn't know about any of these providers. Its provider list is a module-level array built once at import (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:307`), and it only holds credentials, Google, Microsoft and email. Clicking an OIDC button can't start a sign-in, and a provider an admin adds later can't be used without restarting the server.

This is sub-issue **5a** of #131. Sub-issue 5 in the breakdown (PR #133, `specs/oidc-sign-in/breakdown.md`) is split in two so each part can be reviewed and merged on its own:

- **5a (this issue):** the mechanism that registers enabled OIDC providers with NextAuth on each auth request, and a guard that refuses every OIDC sign-in safely until 5b exists. It does not depend on any open PR.
- **5b (next issue):** `OidcSignInService`, which decides who may sign in, creates new users and finds returning users. 5b replaces the guard added here.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Load providers from a provider source on each `/api/auth/*` request and pass them to NextAuth (ADR-001, option 1). The source is an interface defined in this issue; until #136 / PR #155 merges, the handler passes an empty source, so nothing changes on a real instance. Every OIDC sign-in is rejected in `signIn` before any account lookup or write, which keeps the PR safe to merge alone. Behavior is specified in **Acceptance Criteria** below; the planned changes are:

1. `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/buildOidcProvider.ts`: a pure builder that turns one provider record (a local input type) into a next-auth `type: "oauth"` provider: `id: "oidc-<id>"`, `wellKnown`, `idToken: true`, `checks: ["pkce", "state"]`, the provider's scopes, the decrypted secret, **no** `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking` and no `httpOptions`.
2. `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/loadOidcNextAuthProviders.ts`: `loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source)` reads the enabled providers and their encrypted secrets from the source, decrypts with `symmetricDecrypt`, skips a provider that fails, and returns `[]` if the source throws.
3. `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts`: make the handler async, await `loadOidcNextAuthProviders(<empty source>)` and pass the result to `getOptions`.
4. `getOptions` takes an optional `dynamicProviders: Provider[]` (default `[]`) and appends it after the existing providers.
5. **Temporary guard** at the top of the `signIn` callback: any `oidc-*` provider returns `"/auth/error?error=unknown-provider"`. 5b replaces it with the call to `OidcSignInService`.

**Depends on:** nothing open. **Follow-up after #155 merges:** pass `getOidcProviderRepository()` as the source and map `oidc-*` to `IdentityProvider.OIDC`. Blocks 5b.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

The full decisions, each with its alternatives, rationale and consequences, are in **Design** below. In short:

- **How providers reach NextAuth** (ADR-001, PR #133): load on each request (chosen) vs. an in-memory cache invalidated on save (stale on other server instances) vs. building at boot (needs a restart).
- **Independence from #155** (Design, Decision 6): a provider source interface with an empty source until #155 merges (chosen) vs. stacking on #155's branch vs. copying #155's schema and migration vs. a test provider configured from environment variables.
- **Keeping 5a safe to merge alone:** reject every `oidc-*` login at the top of `signIn` (chosen) vs. letting the existing `signIn` branches handle it. The second was rejected because those branches include the "verified and not CAL" path (`next-auth-options.ts:1012`), which can sign into an existing account by email (#131 criterion 28).

### Additional context

- Parent: #131. Sibling sub-issues: #136 (data), #151 (Keycloak), #152 (admin service), #146 (buttons and errors).
- Customer answers on #131 (2026-11-12) that apply: 3 (reject when `email_verified` is missing or false, enforced in 5b) and 13 (no visible change until a provider is added).
- The breakdown asks for a narrow security review of the `signIn` and `jwt` changes in sub-issue 5. For 5a that's only the guard; the full review applies to 5b.
- Open questions are listed under **Open Questions** below.

### Requirement/Document

- Feature spec: PR #133, `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md` (criteria 1, 13, 28; Technical Design, "Each provider becomes a NextAuth `type: \"oauth\"` provider…"), `decisions.md` (ADR-001, ADR-005), `breakdown.md` (sub-issue 5).
- next-auth 4 OAuth provider options: https://next-auth.js.org/configuration/providers/oauth
```

```markdown
# #164 tech debt to carry into the PR description (from design.md, updated 2026-11-19)

## Introduced
- Decision 6: the handler passes an **empty provider source** until #155 merges, so nothing changes on a real instance. Follow-up: pass `getOidcProviderRepository()` as the source and map `oidc-*` to `IdentityProvider.OIDC` in `getIdentityProvider` (needs #155's enum value).
- Decision 6: a local `OidcProviderRecord` / `OidcProviderSource` type mirrors #155's DTOs and repository methods; a one-line `oidc-<id>` helper duplicates #155's `getOidcAccountProviderId`. Remove both when connecting (TypeScript flags a mismatch).
- Decision 1: the handler's one-line call to `loadOidcNextAuthProviders` is not covered by a unit test (Pages API route); the logic itself is tested through the function with a fake source.
- Decision 2: once connected, N+1 reads (`findEnabled()` + `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret(id)` per provider, up to 11 queries per auth request), and the second read doesn't filter on `enabled`. Follow-up: `findEnabledWithEncryptedSecret()` in the repository.
- Decision 3: the temporary refusal reuses `unknown-provider`; 5b removes the guard.
- Decision 4: no explicit timeout (openid-client default 3500 ms) instead of the feature spec's 5000 ms; note on #131 / PR #133.
- Decision 5: providers load on every `/api/auth/*` request, including `session`. Follow-up: filter to `providers`, `signin`, `callback`.

## Encountered
- openid-client HTTP defaults are process-wide (`node_modules/next-auth/node_modules/openid-client/lib/helpers/request.js:17,33-43`), so any provider-level `httpOptions` changes every provider.
```

- comments only for "why".

Ask before schema changes, new dependencies, or changes that span several packages (AGENTS.md).

Ask: **"Approve this plan (or edit it)?"** and stop.

### Step 2 — One step per turn
When the user says to do the next step (or a specific one):
1. Make only that step's edits, code and tests together. Match the surrounding code's style.
2. Then **stop and report**, in this order:
   - **What changed:** each file, with `file:line` and a short snippet of the key lines.
   - **Why.**
   - **Assumptions made.**
   - **How it relates to existing code:** callers and callees, with `file:line`.
   - **What could go wrong:** edge cases and risks.
   - **Tests added or updated,** and what each one proves.
   - **Checks:** run the relevant parts of `/dev-checks` for the touched files (`node .claude/course/scripts/checks-plan.mjs` gives the commands) and report the results. NEW vs pre-existing problems are told apart as in `/dev-checks`.
   - **Files to commit for this step,** plus a **draft commit message** (conventional commit, e.g. `feat(scope): … (#<N>)`), for the user to commit:
     ```bash
     git add <files>
     git commit -m "<message>"
     ```
   - **Running diff size:** `node .claude/course/scripts/pr-facts.mjs`, giving code lines and files so far against the 500 / 10 limit.
   - **A reminder** to check the VS Code Problems panel and to try the change in the running app. The user runs the dev server and E2E.
3. Update `plan.md`: mark the step done and note any change to the plan.

Never go on to the next step in the same turn. If a step turns out bigger or different than planned, stop and re-plan with the user.

### When all steps are done
Suggest `/dev-checks` for a full run, `/dev-explain "last change"` if the user wants a walkthrough, then `/pr-draft <N>`.

```text
import crypto from "node:crypto";

const ALGORITHM = "aes256";
const INPUT_ENCODING = "utf8";
const OUTPUT_ENCODING = "hex";
const IV_LENGTH = 16; // AES blocksize

/**
 *
 * @param text Value to be encrypted
 * @param key Key used to encrypt value must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm
 *
 * @returns Encrypted value using key
 */
export const symmetricEncrypt = function (text: string, key: string) {
  const _key = Buffer.from(key, "latin1");
  const iv = crypto.randomBytes(IV_LENGTH);
  const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv(ALGORITHM, _key, iv);
  let ciphered = cipher.update(text, INPUT_ENCODING, OUTPUT_ENCODING);
  ciphered += cipher.final(OUTPUT_ENCODING);
  const ciphertext = `${iv.toString(OUTPUT_ENCODING)}:${ciphered}`;

  return ciphertext;
};

/**
 *
 * @param text Value to decrypt
 * @param key Key used to decrypt value must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm
 */
export const symmetricDecrypt = function (text: string, key: string) {
  const _key = Buffer.from(key, "latin1");

  const components = text.split(":");
  const iv_from_ciphertext = Buffer.from(components.shift() || "", OUTPUT_ENCODING);
  const decipher = crypto.createDecipheriv(ALGORITHM, _key, iv_from_ciphertext);
  let deciphered = decipher.update(components.join(":"), OUTPUT_ENCODING, INPUT_ENCODING);
  deciphered += decipher.final(INPUT_ENCODING);

  return deciphered;
};
```

```typescript
// Mirrors getOidcAccountProviderId from #136 so this code does not depend on that PR.
// Replace with the repository's helper once #136 is merged.
export const OIDC_PROVIDER_ID_PREFIX = "oidc-";

export function getOidcNextAuthProviderId(id: string): string {
  return `${OIDC_PROVIDER_ID_PREFIX}${id}`;
}

export function isOidcProviderId(provider: string): boolean {
  return provider.startsWith(OIDC_PROVIDER_ID_PREFIX) && provider.length > OIDC_PROVIDER_ID_PREFIX.length;
}
```

```typescript
import type { OAuthConfig } from "next-auth/providers/oauth";

import { getOidcNextAuthProviderId } from "./oidcProviderId";

export interface OidcProviderConfig {
  id: string;
  displayName: string;
  issuer: string;
  clientId: string;
  clientSecret: string;
  scopes: string;
}

export interface OidcProfile {
  sub: string;
  name?: string;
  email?: string;
  picture?: string;
}

export function buildOidcProvider(config: OidcProviderConfig): OAuthConfig<OidcProfile> {
  const issuer = config.issuer.replace(/\/+$/, "");

  // No httpOptions: next-auth applies them as process-wide openid-client defaults,
  // which would also change the timeout for Google and Microsoft (design Decision 4).
  // No allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking: an OIDC login must never attach to an
  // existing account by email (#131 criterion 28).
  return {
    id: getOidcNextAuthProviderId(config.id),
    name: config.displayName,
    type: "oauth",
    issuer,
    wellKnown: `${issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration`,
    clientId: config.clientId,
    clientSecret: config.clientSecret,
    authorization: { params: { scope: config.scopes } },
    idToken: true,
    checks: ["pkce", "state"],
    profile(profile) {
      return {
        id: profile.sub,
        name: profile.name ?? null,
        email: profile.email ?? null,
        image: profile.picture ?? null,
      };
    },
  };
}

```

```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { getOidcNextAuthProviderId, isOidcProviderId, OIDC_PROVIDER_ID_PREFIX } from "./oidcProviderId";

  );

  it("accepts every id built by getOidcNextAuthProviderId", () => {

  });
});
```

```typescript
import type { TokenSet } from "next-auth";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import type { OidcProviderConfig } from "./buildOidcProvider";
import { buildOidcProvider } from "./buildOidcProvider";

const config: OidcProviderConfig = {
  id: "clx123abc",
  displayName: "Acme SSO",
  issuer: "http://localhost:8080/realms/acme",
  clientId: "cal-diy",
  clientSecret: "plain-secret",
  scopes: "openid email profile",
};

describe("buildOidcProvider", () => {
  it("builds an oauth provider with the oidc-<id> id and the display name", () => {
    const provider = buildOidcProvider(config);

    expect(provider.id).toBe("oidc-clx123abc");
    expect(provider.name).toBe("Acme SSO");
    expect(provider.type).toBe("oauth");
  });

  it("uses OIDC discovery from the issuer", () => {
    const provider = buildOidcProvider(config);

    expect(provider.issuer).toBe("http://localhost:8080/realms/acme");
    expect(provider.wellKnown).toBe("http://localhost:8080/realms/acme/.well-known/openid-configuration");
  });

  it("drops trailing slashes from the issuer before building the discovery URL", () => {
    const provider = buildOidcProvider({ ...config, issuer: "https://sso.example.com/realms/acme//" });

    expect(provider.issuer).toBe("https://sso.example.com/realms/acme");
    expect(provider.wellKnown).toBe("https://sso.example.com/realms/acme/.well-known/openid-configuration");
  });

  it("passes the client credentials and the configured scopes", () => {
    const provider = buildOidcProvider({ ...config, scopes: "openid email" });

    expect(provider.clientId).toBe("cal-diy");
    expect(provider.clientSecret).toBe("plain-secret");
    expect(provider.authorization).toEqual({ params: { scope: "openid email" } });
  });

  it("reads the user from the ID token with PKCE and state checks", () => {
    const provider = buildOidcProvider(config);

    expect(provider.idToken).toBe(true);
    expect(provider.checks).toEqual(["pkce", "state"]);
  });

  it("does not allow linking to an existing account by email", () => {
    const provider = buildOidcProvider(config);

    expect(provider).not.toHaveProperty("allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking");
  });

  it("does not set httpOptions, so other providers keep their timeout", () => {
    const provider = buildOidcProvider(config);

    expect(provider).not.toHaveProperty("httpOptions");
  });

  it("maps the ID token claims to a user, using sub as the id", async () => {
    const provider = buildOidcProvider(config);

    const user = await provider.profile(
      { sub: "kc-user-1", name: "Alex Doe", email: "alex@example.com", picture: "https://img/alex.png" },
      {} as TokenSet
    );

    expect(user).toEqual({
      id: "kc-user-1",
      name: "Alex Doe",
      email: "alex@example.com",
      image: "https://img/alex.png",
    });
  });

  it("maps missing optional claims to null", async () => {
    const provider = buildOidcProvider(config);

    const user = await provider.profile({ sub: "kc-user-2" }, {} as TokenSet);

    expect(user).toEqual({ id: "kc-user-2", name: null, email: null, image: null });
  });
});

```

```ts
}
```

**`packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/buildOidcProvider.ts` (new, 47 lines)**
- `OidcProviderConfig` holds `id`, `displayName`, `issuer`, `clientId`, `clientSecret` (plaintext) and `scopes`.
- `buildOidcProvider(config): OAuthConfig<OidcProfile>` returns:
  - `id: oidc-<id>`, `name`, `type: "oauth"`, `issuer`;
  - `wellKnown: <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`, with trailing slashes removed from the issuer first;
  - `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `authorization: { params: { scope } }`;
  - `idToken: true`, `checks: ["pkce", "state"]`;
  - `profile()`, which maps `sub`/`name`/`email`/`picture` to `id`/`name`/`email`/`image` and turns missing claims into `null`.
- A comment explains **why** there's no `httpOptions` (Decision 4) and no `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking` (#131 criterion 28).

**Why:** acceptance criteria 2, 4 and 8, and Decisions 1, 4 and 6. The id helper stands in for #155's `getOidcAccountProviderId`, so this code doesn't depend on that PR.

## Assumptions
- **Setting `issuer` as well as `wellKnown` follows next-auth's own Keycloak provider** (**Unverified** against its source). It's harmless either way: discovery provides the issuer too.
- **A bare `"oidc-"` is not an OIDC id.** There's no real provider id after the prefix, so the guard in step 3 would let it fall through to the existing `unknown-provider` rejection anyway.
- **The `profile()` mapping is deliberately minimal.** A name fallback (e.g. `preferred_username`, #131 criterion 17) belongs to 5b.

## How it relates to existing code
- The provider shape follows next-auth's `OAuthConfig` (`node_modules/next-auth/providers/oauth.d.ts:64-119`, **Confirmed**): `profile` is required, the rest is optional.
- The existing providers are added at module load (`next-auth-options.ts:319-367`, **Confirmed**). This builder's output joins them in step 3.
- Nothing calls these functions yet. Step 2 uses the builder; step 3 uses `isOidcProviderId`.

## What could go wrong
- An issuer with a path but no `/.well-known` support (rare) fails discovery when sign-in starts, not when the provider is built. That's by design (criterion 8).
- If an admin configures scopes without `openid`, discovery still works but no ID token comes back. #152 validates `openid`; this builder doesn't check it.
- `startsWith` is case-sensitive, so `OIDC-1` is not an OIDC id. #155's ids are always generated in lower case.

## Tests
- **`oidcProviderId.test.ts` (13 tests):** the prefix and id format; accepts `oidc-<id>`; rejects `oidc-`, `oidc`, `google`, `azure-ad`, `saml-idp`, `cal`, `xoidc-1`, `OIDC-1` and `""`; and anything the builder's id function produces is recognized as an OIDC id.
- **`buildOidcProvider.test.ts` (9 tests):** id, name and type; discovery URL; trailing-slash issuer; credentials and scope; `idToken` and the PKCE/state checks; no email linking (criterion 4); no `httpOptions` (criterion 8); claim mapping, including missing claims.

```typescript
import { symmetricDecrypt } from "@calcom/lib/crypto";
import logger from "@calcom/lib/logger";
import type { OAuthConfig } from "next-auth/providers/oauth";
import type { OidcProfile } from "./buildOidcProvider";
import { buildOidcProvider } from "./buildOidcProvider";

const log = logger.getSubLogger({ prefix: ["auth", "oidc", "loadOidcNextAuthProviders"] });

// Local shapes that match the repository from #136 (findEnabled / findByIdWithEncryptedSecret),
// so that repository can be passed in unchanged once it is merged (design Decision 6).
export interface OidcProviderRecord {
  id: string;
  displayName: string;
  issuer: string;
  clientId: string;
  scopes: string;
}

export interface OidcProviderRecordWithEncryptedSecret extends OidcProviderRecord {
  clientSecretEncrypted: string;
}

export interface OidcProviderSource {
  findEnabled(): Promise<OidcProviderRecord[]>;
  findByIdWithEncryptedSecret(id: string): Promise<OidcProviderRecordWithEncryptedSecret | null>;
}

export const emptyOidcProviderSource: OidcProviderSource = {
  findEnabled: async () => [],
  findByIdWithEncryptedSecret: async () => null,
};

/**
 * Never throws: a failure here would break every sign-in method, so problems are logged
 * and the affected OIDC providers are left out instead.
 */
export async function loadOidcNextAuthProviders(
  source: OidcProviderSource,
  encryptionKey: string | undefined = process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY
): Promise<OAuthConfig<OidcProfile>[]> {
  let enabled: OidcProviderRecord[];
  try {
    enabled = await source.findEnabled();
  } catch (error) {
    log.warn("Could not load OIDC providers; continuing without them", {
      error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
    });
    return [];
  }

  if (enabled.length === 0) return [];

  if (!encryptionKey) {
    log.warn("CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set; OIDC providers are disabled", {
      providerIds: enabled.map((provider) => provider.id),
    });
    return [];
  }

  const providers: OAuthConfig<OidcProfile>[] = [];
  for (const { id } of enabled) {
    try {
      const record = await source.findByIdWithEncryptedSecret(id);
      if (!record) {
        log.warn("OIDC provider disappeared while loading; skipping it", { providerId: id });
        continue;
      }
      providers.push(
        buildOidcProvider({
          id: record.id,
          displayName: record.displayName,
          issuer: record.issuer,
          clientId: record.clientId,
          clientSecret: symmetricDecrypt(record.clientSecretEncrypted, encryptionKey),
          scopes: record.scopes,
        })
      );
    } catch {
      // The error is not logged: a decryption error message could include key or ciphertext details.
      log.warn("Could not load OIDC provider secret; skipping it", { providerId: id });
    }
  }
  return providers;
}
```
