```typescript
import { symmetricEncrypt } from "@calcom/lib/crypto";
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import type {
  OidcProviderRecord,
  OidcProviderRecordWithEncryptedSecret,
  OidcProviderSource,
} from "./loadOidcNextAuthProviders";
import { emptyOidcProviderSource, loadOidcNextAuthProviders } from "./loadOidcNextAuthProviders";

const { mockWarn } = vi.hoisted(() => ({ mockWarn: vi.fn() }));

vi.mock("@calcom/lib/logger", () => ({
  default: { getSubLogger: () => ({ warn: mockWarn }) },
}));

const KEY = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef";
const WRONG_KEY = "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210";

function record(id: string, displayName = `Provider ${id}`): OidcProviderRecord {
  return {
    id,
    displayName,
    issuer: `https://sso.example.com/realms/${id}`,
    clientId: `client-${id}`,
    scopes: "openid email profile",
  };
}

function withSecret(r: OidcProviderRecord, secret: string, key = KEY): OidcProviderRecordWithEncryptedSecret {
  return { ...r, clientSecretEncrypted: symmetricEncrypt(secret, key) };
}

function fakeSource(rows: OidcProviderRecordWithEncryptedSecret[]): OidcProviderSource {
  return {
    findEnabled: vi.fn(async () => rows.map(({ clientSecretEncrypted: _secret, ...rest }) => rest)),
    findByIdWithEncryptedSecret: vi.fn(async (id: string) => rows.find((row) => row.id === id) ?? null),
  };
}

function loggedText(): string {
  return JSON.stringify(mockWarn.mock.calls);
}

describe("loadOidcNextAuthProviders", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    mockWarn.mockReset();
  });

  it("returns no providers for the empty source", async () => {
    expect(await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(emptyOidcProviderSource, KEY)).toEqual([]);
    expect(mockWarn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("builds one provider per enabled record, in the source's order, with the decrypted secret", async () => {
    const source = fakeSource([withSecret(record("b", "Beta"), "secret-b"), withSecret(record("a", "Alpha"), "secret-a")]);

    const providers = await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source, KEY);

    expect(providers.map((p) => [p.id, p.name, p.type])).toEqual([
      ["oidc-b", "Beta", "oauth"],
      ["oidc-a", "Alpha", "oauth"],
    ]);
    expect(providers.map((p) => p.clientSecret)).toEqual(["secret-b", "secret-a"]);
    expect(providers[0].wellKnown).toBe("https://sso.example.com/realms/b/.well-known/openid-configuration");
  });

  it("reads the source again on every call, so changes need no restart", async () => {
    const rows = [withSecret(record("a"), "secret-a")];
    const source = fakeSource(rows);

    expect((await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source, KEY)).map((p) => p.id)).toEqual(["oidc-a"]);

    rows.push(withSecret(record("b"), "secret-b"));
    expect((await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source, KEY)).map((p) => p.id)).toEqual(["oidc-a", "oidc-b"]);

    rows.splice(0, 2);
    expect(await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source, KEY)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("returns no providers and warns when the source throws", async () => {
    const source: OidcProviderSource = {
      findEnabled: vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error("database is down")),
      findByIdWithEncryptedSecret: vi.fn(),
    };

    expect(await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source, KEY)).toEqual([]);
    expect(mockWarn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(source.findByIdWithEncryptedSecret).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("skips only the provider whose secret cannot be decrypted", async () => {
    const source = fakeSource([
      withSecret(record("bad"), "secret-bad", WRONG_KEY),
      withSecret(record("good"), "secret-good"),
    ]);

    const providers = await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source, KEY);

    expect(providers.map((p) => p.id)).toEqual(["oidc-good"]);
    expect(mockWarn).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.any(String), { providerId: "bad" });
  });

  it("skips a provider whose record is gone when its secret is read", async () => {
    const source = fakeSource([withSecret(record("a"), "secret-a"), withSecret(record("b"), "secret-b")]);
    vi.mocked(source.findByIdWithEncryptedSecret).mockImplementationOnce(async () => null);

    const providers = await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source, KEY);

    expect(providers.map((p) => p.id)).toEqual(["oidc-b"]);
    expect(mockWarn).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.any(String), { providerId: "a" });
  });

  it("returns no providers and warns when the encryption key is missing", async () => {
    const source = fakeSource([withSecret(record("a"), "secret-a")]);

    expect(await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source, undefined)).toEqual([]);
    expect(await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source, "")).toEqual([]);
    expect(mockWarn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(source.findByIdWithEncryptedSecret).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("never logs a secret or its ciphertext", async () => {
    const bad = withSecret(record("bad"), "top-secret-bad", WRONG_KEY);
    const good = withSecret(record("good"), "top-secret-good");

    await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(fakeSource([bad, good]), KEY);
    await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(fakeSource([good]), undefined);

    expect(mockWarn).toHaveBeenCalled();
    const text = loggedText();
    for (const value of ["top-secret-bad", "top-secret-good", bad.clientSecretEncrypted, good.clientSecretEncrypted, KEY]) {
      expect(text).not.toContain(value);
    }
  });
});
```

```bash
  };

  beforeEach(async () => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();

  });

    getOptions(baseArgs).callbacks!.signIn!({
      user: { id: "kc-user-1", email: "admin@example.com", emailVerified: new Date() },
      account: { provider, type: "oauth", providerAccountId: "kc-user-1" },
      profile: { sub: "kc-user-1", email: "admin@example.com", email_verified: true },
    } as SignInParams);

  it("rejects every oidc-* sign-in with unknown-provider before any lookup or write", async () => {
    const result = await runSignIn("oidc-clx123abc");

    expect(result).toBe("/auth/error?error=unknown-provider");
    expect(mockGetIdentityProvider).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(mockPrismaUserFindFirst).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(mockPrismaUserCreate).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(mockPrismaUserUpdate).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(mockLinkAccount).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("still sends other OAuth providers through the existing identity provider lookup", async () => {
    await runSignIn("google");

    expect(mockGetIdentityProvider).toHaveBeenCalledWith("google");
  });

  it("keeps the built-in providers unchanged when no dynamic providers are passed", () => {
    const withoutArg = getOptions(baseArgs).providers;
    const withEmpty = getOptions({ ...baseArgs, dynamicProviders: [] }).providers;

    expect(withEmpty).toEqual(withoutArg);
    expect(withoutArg.some((provider) => provider?.id?.startsWith("oidc-"))).toBe(false);
  });

  it("adds dynamic providers after the built-in ones", () => {
    const builtIn = getOptions(baseArgs).providers;
    const providers = getOptions({ ...baseArgs, dynamicProviders: [oidcProvider] }).providers;

    expect(providers).toHaveLength(builtIn.length + 1);
    expect(providers.slice(0, builtIn.length)).toEqual(builtIn);
    expect(providers[providers.length - 1]).toBe(oidcProvider);
  });

  it("does not keep dynamic providers between calls", () => {
    getOptions({ ...baseArgs, dynamicProviders: [oidcProvider] });

    expect(getOptions(baseArgs).providers).not.toContain(oidcProvider);
  });
});
```

```typescript
import type { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from "next";
import NextAuth from "next-auth";

import { getOptions } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options";
import {
  emptyOidcProviderSource,
  loadOidcNextAuthProviders,
} from "@calcom/features/auth/oidc/lib/loadOidcNextAuthProviders";
import { getTrackingFromCookies } from "@calcom/lib/tracking";

// pass req to NextAuth: https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/discussions/469
const handler = async (req: NextApiRequest, res: NextApiResponse) => {
  // Loaded per request so admin changes apply without a restart (ADR-001). The source stays empty
  // until the OIDC provider repository from #136 is merged; then pass getOidcProviderRepository() here.
  const dynamicProviders = await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(
    emptyOidcProviderSource,
    process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY
  );

  return NextAuth(
    req,
    res,
    getOptions({
      getDubId: () => req.cookies.dub_id || req.cookies.dclid,
      getTrackingData: () => getTrackingFromCookies(req.cookies, req.query),
      dynamicProviders,
    })
  );
};

export default handler;
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-20 05:19:05Z)**_

Steps 2–4 are written and all 87 related tests pass. `@calcom/feature-auth` type-checks clean, but **`@calcom/web` has one type error, in my step 1 builder**. Fixing it needs a small typing decision from you.

## The type error
```
buildOidcProvider.ts:38:5 - error TS2322: ... Types of property 'id' are incompatible.
  Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'.
```
- **The app's next-auth augmentation types `User.id` as the Prisma user id, a number** (`packages/types/next-auth.d.ts:19-20`, **Confirmed**). Only `apps/web` includes that file (`apps/web/tsconfig.json`), which is why `@calcom/feature-auth` passed.
- **next-auth itself treats `profile().id` as the provider's account id.** It runs `providerAccountId: profile.id.toString()` (`node_modules/next-auth/core/lib/oauth/callback.js:149`, **Confirmed**). Returning the OIDC `sub` (a string) is correct at runtime; the augmented type just doesn't describe this case.
- **The existing Azure provider returns `id: profile.sub` the same way** (`next-auth-options.ts:352-358`). It passes on `main`, but failed in my scratch type-check (since deleted). I couldn't work out why: **Unverified**. So I can't just copy its pattern with confidence.

## Options

| | **A. One explicit, commented conversion** | **B. Loosen the claims type, like next-auth's built-in providers** |
|---|---|---|
| Change | In `profile()`: `id: profile.sub as unknown as User["id"]`, with a comment citing `callback.js:149` and the augmentation. | `OidcProfile` becomes `Record<string, any>` without a declared `sub`, the same shape as `AzureADProfile` (`node_modules/next-auth/providers/azure-ad.d.ts:2`). `profile.sub` is then `any` and assigns without a cast. |
| Pros | Claims stay strictly typed; the mismatch is stated in one place. `User["id"]` is right in both packages (string without the augmentation, number with it). | No type assertion in the code. Matches how next-auth types its own providers. |
| Cons | A double cast, which a reviewer may question. Not `as any`, so it doesn't break that rule (AGENTS.md), but it is a type escape. | An explicit `any` type: `sub`, `name`, `email` and `picture` lose their types, and Biome may warn about it. Goes against the spirit of "no `as any`" (AGENTS.md). |
| Tests | Unchanged | Unchanged |

There's also a third route: fix the augmentation itself so OAuth profiles may have a string id. It's out of scope: it changes a type the whole app uses and would touch many files.

**Which do you choose, A or B?** If you want a recommendation: A, moderately confident. It keeps the claims typed, and the one cast is documented by next-auth's own runtime code.

When it's fixed, I'll rerun the `@calcom/web` type-check, then give you the commit commands for steps 2–4 and the full step-by-step report.

## What changed

**Step 2: `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/loadOidcNextAuthProviders.ts` (new, 84 lines)**
- **Types:** `OidcProviderRecord`, `OidcProviderRecordWithEncryptedSecret` and `OidcProviderSource`. They're named after #155's repository methods so the repository can be passed in unchanged later. Also `emptyOidcProviderSource`.
- **`loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source, encryptionKey)` never throws.** It:
  - returns `[]` with a warning if `findEnabled()` throws, or if the key is missing and at least one provider is enabled;
  - otherwise reads each provider's secret, decrypts it with `symmetricDecrypt` and builds the provider, in the source's order;
  - skips a provider whose record is gone or whose decryption fails, warning with `{ providerId }` only. The caught error isn't logged, so key or ciphertext details can't leak.

**Step 3: `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (+15 / −1)**
- `getOptions` takes an optional `dynamicProviders: Provider[] = []`, and its provider list is now `providers: [...providers, ...dynamicProviders]`.
- The guard comes right after the `signIn` destructuring, before every other branch:
  ```ts
  if (account?.provider && isOidcProviderId(account.provider)) {
    log.warn("callbacks:signIn - OIDC sign-in is not available yet, rejecting login", { provider: account.provider });
    return "/auth/error?error=unknown-provider";
  }
  ```
  A three-line comment explains why the guard exists (5b, criterion 28, and next-auth running `signIn` before any write).

**Step 4: `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts` (+15 / −2)**
- The handler is now async. It calls `await loadOidcNextAuthProviders(emptyOidcProviderSource, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` and passes the result as `dynamicProviders`.
- A comment says why the source is empty and what to pass once #155 merges.

**Fix in step 1's builder: `buildOidcProvider.ts:40-44`**
- `id: profile.sub as unknown as User["id"]`, with a comment citing next-auth's `callback.js` and the app's augmentation.

**Why:** acceptance criteria 1, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 9, and Decisions 1, 3, 5 and 6.

## Assumptions
- **The encryption key is a required argument.** My first version read it from the environment as a default parameter, so passing `undefined` silently fell back to the environment value. The test caught it.
- **Secrets are read one provider at a time,** not in parallel. With at most 10 providers this is simple and fine for now; it's part of Decision 2's tech debt.
- **The guard runs before the existing `log.debug(params)`,** so OIDC profiles aren't written to debug logs.

## How it relates to existing code
- **The guard sits before** the `email` and credentials early returns (`next-auth-options.ts:837-855`), the name check (`:861`), `getIdentityProvider` (`:869`), and the email-based branches its comment refers to.
- **The two other `getOptions` callers still compile unchanged:** `license-key/new/getServerSideProps.tsx:10` and the existing tests.
- **The handler now uses the loader** from `loadOidcNextAuthProviders.ts`, which uses the step 1 builder.

## What could go wrong
- **Every auth request awaits the loader.** With the empty source that's one resolved promise, so the cost is negligible until the repository is connected (Decision 5's tech debt).
- **An OIDC provider whose id is `oidc-…` never reaches account logic** until 5b replaces the guard. That's intended, but 5b must remove the guard.
- **The `as unknown as User["id"]` cast** hides any future change to next-auth's profile contract. The comment points to where to re-check it.
- **Why the Azure provider type-checks on `main` is still unexplained** (**Unverified**).

## Tests
- **`loadOidcNextAuthProviders.test.ts` (8):**
  - empty source;
  - order kept and secrets decrypted, using real `symmetricEncrypt`;
  - per-call reload, with providers added and removed;
  - a source that throws gives `[]`;
  - a malformed ciphertext skips only that provider;
  - a missing record skips only that provider;
  - a missing key (`undefined` and `""`) gives `[]`;
  - no secret, ciphertext or key appears in any warning.

  The malformed-ciphertext test uses a malformed value rather than a wrong key, because a wrong key decrypts to garbage about 1 time in 256 and would make the test flaky.
- **`next-auth-options.test.ts`, new `OIDC providers (#164)` block (5):**
  - `oidc-*` gets `unknown-provider` with no identity lookup, no user read/create/update and no account link, even for a verified email matching an ADMIN;
  - Google still reaches `getIdentityProvider`;
  - with no dynamic providers, the provider list is unchanged and contains no `oidc-*`;
  - dynamic providers are appended last;
  - nothing carries over between calls.
- **Step 4** has no route test, as planned (Decision 1's tech debt).

```text
## What does this PR do?

Closes #146

Sub-issue 6 of #131 (OIDC sign-in). Adds the login and sign-up buttons for admin-configured OIDC providers and makes sign-in failures visible. It depends on #136 for the provider data: until #136 merges, both pages receive an empty provider list, so **nothing changes on screen except the error messages** (see Tech Debt).

### What changed

- **Shared error-message mapping:** `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/authErrorMessages.ts`
  - `getLoginErrorMessage` (`:26`) maps NextAuth's sign-in-page codes: `OAuthSignin` → provider unreachable; `OAuthCallback` / `Callback` → sign-in failed; anything else → a generic message (`:6-10`).
  - `getAuthErrorPageMessage` (`:46`) holds the existing `/auth/error` messages unchanged, plus `AccessDenied`, `missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists` and `unknown-provider` (`:12-21`). It names OIDC accounts as "single sign-on" in `wrong-provider` (`:39`).
  - Lookups use `Map`, so a code like `constructor` can't match a built-in object property.
- **`/auth/error` uses the module:** `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx:36` replaces the old if/else chain.
- **The login page reads `?error=`:** `apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx`
  - keeps the code in state (`:132`) and shows the translated message in the existing alert (`:181-182`, `:341-343`);
  - submitting the email form clears it;
  - this applies to Google and Microsoft failures too. Before, the page ignored `error` completely.
- **Provider-button mapping:** `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/oidcLoginButtons.ts`
  - `toOidcLoginButtons` (`:26`) and `toOidcSignupButtons` (`:30`) copy only `id` and `displayName` into page props;
  - the sign-up version keeps only providers with `allowSignup` and returns nothing when sign-up is disabled;
  - `getOidcSignInProviderId` (`:16`) builds the NextAuth id `oidc-<id>`.
- **Login buttons:**
  - `login-view.tsx:244-264`: one "Continue with <name>" button per provider, after Microsoft. Clicking it records `oidc-<id>` as last used and calls `signIn("oidc-<id>", { callbackUrl })`;
  - `showSocialLogin` (`:184`) now counts OIDC providers, so an instance with only OIDC configured still shows the buttons and the divider;
  - server props: `apps/web/server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx:90`, `:97`;
  - `useLastUsed.tsx:9` accepts `oidc-<id>`.
- **Sign-up buttons:**
  - `apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx:737-752`, divider condition at `:754`;
  - server props: `apps/web/lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx:59-68`. These apply `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_SIGNUP` / `disable-signup` too, because invite links with a token still render the sign-up page when the env var is set.
- **Strings:** 10 keys in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:4847-4856`.

### Why

The login and sign-up pages could only show the hard-coded Google and Microsoft buttons, so users had no way to reach an OIDC provider. Sign-in failures were also invisible: NextAuth redirects failed OAuth sign-ins to `/auth/login?error=…` (`next-auth/core/index.js:209-214`), but `login-view.tsx` never read `error`.

This PR meets acceptance criteria 1–9 of #146. Criteria 1, 4 and 5 are fully visible only once #136 supplies real providers; the logic is tested now with sample data.

### Design

Design decisions for #146 (sub-issue 6 of #131). Each follows the course template.

#### Decision 1: Where error-code messages live

**Decision:** Map sign-in error codes to translation keys in one shared pure module, `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/authErrorMessages.ts`, used by both the login page and `/auth/error`.

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Shared pure module (chosen): `getLoginErrorKey(code)` and `getAuthErrorPageMessage(code, provider)` return i18n keys and parameters; `login-view.tsx` and `auth/error/page.tsx` call them, and a `.test.ts` file covers every code plus an unknown one.
2. Extend each page in place: add entries to the `errorMessages` map in `login-view.tsx` (`:131-137`) and new branches to the if/else chain in `auth/error/page.tsx` (`:36-56`).
3. Add NextAuth's codes (`OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback`, …) to the `ErrorCode` enum in `packages/features/auth/lib/ErrorCode.ts` and look them up in the login page's existing map.

**Rationale:** It keeps the mapping in one place that a unit test can reach and avoids duplicating the logic across two pages. A pure function can be tested with plain inputs. Logic left inside the views would need component tests with rendering and mocks, and the `/auth/error` server page under `apps/web/app/` has no Vitest project that collects its tests (`vitest.workspace.ts` only collects `.tsx` tests from `apps/web/modules/**` and `apps/web/components/**`, `:158`, `:188`), so its logic could only be checked manually; the enum option would put web-only NextAuth codes into `packages/features` and still not help `/auth/error`.

**Consequences:** Easier: unit tests for acceptance criteria 6–8, a clear target for StrykerJS mutation testing (D6), and adding future codes in one place. Harder: one new file and one more level of indirection; the pages still need a manual check that they display the returned key.

#### Decision 2: How providers reach the pages before #136

**Decision:** Pass providers to the login and sign-up pages as an `oidcProviders` prop of `{ id, displayName }` built by a pure mapper, with the props set to `[]` until #136 merges and the `findEnabled()` call added as a final commit.

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Props + mapper now, wire later (chosen): add `OidcLoginButton` (`{ id, displayName }`) and `toOidcLoginButtons(providers, { signup })`, which filters by `allowSignup` and drops every other field; `server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx` and `lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx` pass the result; the input type temporarily copies the shape of #136's `OidcProviderPublicDto`.
```

````markdown
## What does this PR do?

Closes #164

Sub-issue 5a of #131 (OIDC sign-in). Adds the mechanism that registers admin-configured OIDC providers with NextAuth on every auth request, and a guard that safely refuses every OIDC sign-in until account handling (5b) exists. It does not depend on any open PR: the handler uses an **empty provider source** until #136 / PR #155 merges, so **nothing changes on a running instance yet** (see Tech Debt).

### What changed

- **Provider id helpers:** `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/oidcProviderId.ts`
  - `getOidcNextAuthProviderId(id)` (`:5`) builds `oidc-<id>`; `isOidcProviderId(provider)` (`:9`) is true only for `oidc-` followed by an id.
- **Pure provider builder:** `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/buildOidcProvider.ts`
  - `buildOidcProvider(config)` (`:21`) returns a next-auth `oauth` provider: `id: oidc-<id>`, the display name, `issuer` and `wellKnown` discovery URL (trailing slashes removed), client id and secret, the configured scopes, `idToken: true`, `checks: ["pkce", "state"]`, and a `profile()` that maps `sub` / `name` / `email` / `picture`.
  - It sets **no** `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking` and **no** `httpOptions`; a comment explains why (`:24-27`).
- **Loader with a provider source:** `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/loadOidcNextAuthProviders.ts`
  - `OidcProviderSource` (`:23`) uses the same method names as #155's repository (`findEnabled`, `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret`), so the repository can be passed in unchanged later; `emptyOidcProviderSource` (`:28`).
  - `loadOidcNextAuthProviders(source, encryptionKey)` (`:37`) never throws. It returns `[]` if the source throws (`:45-48`) or the key is missing (`:54-57`), and skips one provider whose record is gone (`:65`) or whose secret can't be decrypted (`:80`). Warnings carry only the provider id, never the secret.
- **NextAuth options:** `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`
  - `getOptions` takes an optional `dynamicProviders` (`:382`, `:389`) and appends them after the built-in providers (`:424`). Existing callers are unchanged.
  - **Guard** at the top of `signIn` (`:828-833`): any `oidc-*` provider returns `/auth/error?error=unknown-provider` before every lookup or write.
- **Route handler:** `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts:12-29` is now async, loads providers per request from the empty source and passes them to `getOptions`.

### Why

The OIDC buttons from #146 call `signIn("oidc-<id>")`, but NextAuth's provider list is a module-level array built once at import (`next-auth-options.ts:307`), so those providers can never start a sign-in, and a new provider would need a restart. Registering them blindly would be unsafe: the existing `signIn` branches can match an existing account by email (`next-auth-options.ts:1012`, #131 criterion 28), so this PR refuses every OIDC sign-in until 5b decides who may sign in. next-auth calls `signIn` before it creates or links any account (`node_modules/next-auth/core/routes/callback.js:78` before `:104`), so a refused login writes nothing.

This PR meets acceptance criteria 1–10 of #164. Criteria 1, 2 and 8 are proven with a fake provider source; their live checks against Keycloak wait until the repository is connected (Out of Scope in #164).

**Size note:** 518 lines in 9 code files, 18 lines over the 500-line guideline (AGENTS.md); about 60% of the lines are tests (see Tech Debt).

### Design

Six decisions, each with alternatives, rationale and consequences, are in the `## Design` section of #164. In short:

1. **Where the logic lives:** a pure builder plus a loader function, called from a thin route handler. Rejected: a DI service (more files for one method) and an async `getOptions` (breaks the synchronous caller in `apps/web/lib/settings/license-key/new/getServerSideProps.tsx:10` and 8 test call sites).
2. **Reading secrets:** #155's existing methods (`findEnabled` + `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret`) once connected. Rejected: asking for or adding a new repository method in #155 (couples this PR to an open one).
3. **Refusal code:** reuse `unknown-provider`, whose message already exists. Rejected: a new `oidc-not-available` code (new string, depends on #161) and returning `false` (next-auth shows `AccessDenied`, which is misleading).
4. **Timeout:** no `httpOptions`, because next-auth applies them as process-wide openid-client defaults and would change Google and Microsoft too. Rejected: the spec's literal 5000 ms.
5. **When to load:** on every `/api/auth/*` request (ADR-001). Rejected for now: only the `providers`, `signin` and `callback` actions.
6. **Independence from #155:** a provider source interface with an empty source. Rejected: stacking on #155's branch, copying its schema and migration, and a test provider from environment variables.

## Visual Demo (For contributors especially)

No visible change is expected: the provider source is empty until #155 merges.

## How should this be tested?

- **Environment variables:** `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` as usual (the loader only reads it when a provider is enabled). No new variables.
- **Test data:** none. The provider source is empty, so no OIDC provider or Keycloak is needed.
- **Expected:** every existing sign-in method behaves as before; `/api/auth/providers` lists no `oidc-*` provider.

### Test strategy

- **Unit, `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/oidcProviderId.test.ts` (13):** id format; which provider ids count as OIDC.
- **Unit, `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/buildOidcProvider.test.ts` (9):** id, name and type; discovery URL and trailing slashes; credentials and scope; ID token, PKCE and state; no email linking; no `httpOptions`; claim mapping, including missing claims.
- **Unit, `packages/features/auth/oidc/lib/loadOidcNextAuthProviders.test.ts` (8), fake source and real `symmetricEncrypt`:** empty source; order and decryption; reload on every call; source throws; malformed secret skips one; missing record skips one; missing key; no secret, ciphertext or key in any warning.
- **Unit, `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.test.ts`, new `OIDC providers (#164)` block (5):** the guard refuses `oidc-*` with no lookup, read, write or account link, even for a verified email that matches an ADMIN; Google still reaches the identity provider lookup; providers unchanged without dynamic providers; dynamic providers appended last; nothing kept between calls. The 44 existing tests in the file still pass.
- **Manual:** the dev-server checks below.
````

_**User (2026-11-20 05:42:21Z)**_

AFter running git merge origin/main, the MERGE_MSG screen popped up. What does it mean, and what should be done?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-20 05:42:30Z)**_

That screen means the merge worked. Git just wants a message for the **merge commit** it's about to create. Because your branch and `main` both had new commits, git can't simply move your branch forward, so it makes a commit that joins the two histories. It pre-fills a default message, `Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into feat/issue-164-oidc-provider-registration`, and opens your editor in case you want to change it.

**Keep the default message: just save and close.** How depends on which editor opened:

- **Vim** (a bare terminal screen, lines starting with `~`, `MERGE_MSG` at the bottom): press `Esc`, type `:wq`, press `Enter`.
- **Nano** (shortcuts like `^X Exit` at the bottom): press `Ctrl+O`, then `Enter` to save, then `Ctrl+X` to exit.
- **VS Code** (a `MERGE_MSG` tab opened): save it (`Ctrl+S`) and close the tab. The terminal waits until the tab is closed.

The lines starting with `#` are comments; git ignores them.

**Check that it worked:**
```bash
git log --oneline -3   # the top line should be "Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' ..."
git status             # should say your branch is ahead of origin and the working tree is clean (apart from the files you're leaving out)
```

**If you'd rather cancel the merge:** in Vim, type `:cq` instead of `:wq`. Or delete the uncommented message line, save and close; git aborts when the message is empty. Then run `git merge --abort` if git says a merge is still in progress.

**To skip this screen next time:** `git merge --no-edit origin/main` uses the default message without opening the editor.

After that, push as planned with `git push -u origin feat/issue-164-oidc-provider-registration`. The two merged commits are docs only, so there's no need to rerun the checks.
